findings.rule: When printing ABI-encoded event data or call arguments, map each head word that is an offset into the tail to its own field (length word + data at that offset), in head order.

notes: All 25 ABI functions compared, the batch functions and hooks in full. No semantic error found (approval checks, length mismatch, zero address, paused check, balance checks, the receiver hook's three outcomes). Loops: the five source loops are readable whiles: balanceOfBatch, _safeBatchTransferFrom, _mintBatch, _burnBatch, and Strings.toHexString (2 copies in grantRole and in revokeRole). The only other while is balanceOfBatch's address[] decoding. Thanks to Cancun's MCOPY the ABI encodings are copy lines, no P7. P4: balanceOf[concat(mem[32 * s + 160])][from] keys in the batch loops (12 lines); P11: the 'if s >= ids.length' bounds checks implied by the loop tests; P8: dead hash-buffer writes (mem[0]/mem[32]).
summary: Clean and faithful ERC1155 text with every source loop readable; the one real defect is that events and calls with several dynamic arrays print the later arrays as their head offsets.
